headline: PhilGEPS Witness Says GenCorp Won 49 Government Contracts Worth ₱35.88 Million During Sara Duterte’s VP Term
seoTitle: PhilGEPS Witness Details 49 GenCorp Government Contracts During Sara Duterte VP Term | FMB News
seoDescription: A PhilGEPS official testified that GenCorp Industries, a company Sara Duterte declared as a business interest, received 49 government contracts worth ₱35.88 million from July 2022 to June 2026.
deck: Procurement official Rendell Sopeña testified that PhilGEPS records show 49 awards to GenCorp from Davao City, PhilHealth Region XI and OWWA Region XI during Duterte’s vice-presidential term. The records are evidence in the prosecution case, not a finding that Duterte personally received the contract proceeds or violated the Constitution.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System division chief Rendell Sopeña testified on Day 28 of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial that a search of the government procurement repository found 49 contracts awarded to GenCorp Industries Inc. during Duterte’s term as vice president.

The contracts totaled ₱35,878,188. According to Sopeña’s testimony, Davao City awarded 15 contracts worth ₱34,216,900, PhilHealth Region XI awarded 33 worth ₱1,331,288, and OWWA Region XI awarded one worth ₱330,000.

sections.heading: What is confirmed
paragraphs: The House of Representatives’ official prosecution release records Sopeña’s testimony and the contract totals. GMA News, Philstar, PNA and BusinessMirror independently report the same PhilGEPS evidence and substantially matching figures.

The procurement records covered awards from July 2022 through June 2026, overlapping Duterte’s term as vice president. Duterte had declared GenCorp as a business interest in her SALNs, according to evidence already presented in the impeachment trial.

sections.heading: What is alleged or disputed
paragraphs: The House prosecution argues that the procurement records are relevant to its allegation that Duterte failed to divest business and financial interests while in office. That is the prosecution’s legal theory, not a finding by the Senate impeachment court.

The defense noted that the contracts were awarded after Duterte had left the Davao City mayoralty. Defense counsel also questioned aspects of the prosecution’s presentation of the PhilGEPS material. Separately, Davao City Mayor Sebastian Duterte has said city officials were unaware of any interest the Vice President allegedly held in GenCorp and has maintained that the city’s transactions were above board.

The existence and value of contracts do not by themselves establish that Sara Duterte personally received the contract proceeds, participated in procurement decisions, or committed an impeachable offense. Those issues remain unresolved and subject to the evidentiary and legal process.

sections.heading: Continuation
paragraphs: This is a new evidentiary development in the same Article II sequence covered by FMB News on September 22. Earliest relevant FMB News report: /news/sara-duterte-impeachment-saln-day-25-september-15-2026. Previous continuation: /news/sara-duterte-sec-director-impeachment-day-27-september-22-2026.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: The testimony adds government procurement records to the prosecution’s existing SALN and corporate-record evidence. The central unresolved question is not simply whether GenCorp had government contracts, but what financial interest Duterte legally held, if any, during her vice presidency and whether the evidence satisfies the constitutional and impeachment standards being argued before the Senate.

verificationNotes: The House’s official September 22 release documents PhilGEPS division chief Rendell Sopeña’s open-court testimony and the 49-contract, ₱35,878,188 total.
GMA, Philstar, PNA and BusinessMirror independently corroborate the procurement testimony and breakdown.

The article distinguishes the existence of GenCorp contracts from the prosecution’s allegation that Duterte maintained a prohibited financial interest; no personal receipt of contract proceeds is asserted.
The defense and Davao City mayor’s positions are included, and the article does not treat prosecution characterization as a Senate finding.
